newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African 1996 gold output lowest in 40 years.
newsitem.headline: South African 1996 gold output lowest in 40 years.

text.p: Gold production in South Africa, the world's largest gold producer, plunged to a 40-year low of 495 metric tons last year but production should stabilise at about 500 tons a year in the future, the Chamber of Mines said Monday.
Gold output fell by 27.8 tons to 494.62 tons last year, only marginally higher than the 494.44 tons produced in 1956, the chamber said.

South African gold output has been declining steadily, with rising working costs and dwindling grades chipping away at production, but Chamber of Mines senior economist Roger Baxter said he did not expect the situation to get any worse.
"We can see that the rate of decline in the industry, the rate of fall in production, is stabilising," he said.
Baxter said output had dropped from 619 tonnes in 1993 to 584 tonnes in 1994 and 522 tonnes in 1995.
"The rate of fall-off in production has definitely turned and production levels are expected to stabilise at roughly the 500 tons level for the foreseeable future," Baxter said.
He said reasons for the drop in production included workplace disruptions, consolidation in the industry, escalating costs and a focus on quality mining at the expense of quantity.
